purpose: Desktop web application for building road networks and running agent-based traffic simulations in Three.js

coordinates.unit: World unit = 1/4 road tile (one City Kit Roads tile scaled ×4 = 4 units). Real-world metres not yet assigned.
coordinates.forwardAxis: +Z for vehicles (Car Kit front wheels at +Z). City Kit road-straight runs along X in source; rotated 90° about Y to run along Z.
coordinates.originPolicy: Car Kit: origin at ground centre of vehicle. City Kit Roads: origin at tile centre, surface at y=0.02 (source units). App keeps source origins and places by transform. Scene ground: a 64 × 64 unit square board (16 × 16 road tiles), rounded corners (r = 4), 0.4 thick + 0.2 bevel above and below (0.8 visible edge), centred on the origin with its top face at y = 0; roads and vehicles sit on that top face.
coordinates.conversionPolicy: Inspect source units and axes, confirm the application's conventions, and record conversions before applying them.
coordinates.simulationUnits: Traffic simulation in metres and seconds; 1 tile = 8.75 m (lane 0.4 tile = 3.5 m)

deliveryFormats: GLB with external PNG texture (Textures/colormap.png beside each model)
externalDependencies: public/models/roads/Textures/colormap.png (City Kit Roads; different file, same name)

roadPieces.source: assets/3d/source/kenney_city-kit-roads/Models/GLB format/*.glb (17 road pieces + tile-high + 3 control props)

vehicles.scale: type length in metres / 8.75 m per tile × 4 units per tile; width capped at 75% of a lane

roadPieces.placementPreview: Use a translucent preview with the same position, rotation, elevation, snapping, and validity checks as the final placement.
roadPieces.gradeSeparation: Roads at different heights connect through an explicit link, such as a ramp.
roadPieces.metadataSource: src/simulation/network/pieces.ts (ports measured from the GLB geometry: an opening is an edge with kerbs at both ends of a 0.8-tile carriageway)
roadPieces.sceneFormat: src/simulation/network/scene.ts (board tiles: x east, z south, origin at the north-west corner; half tiles allowed; quarter-turn rotations anticlockwise from above; optional base level and per-port one-way flow)
roadPieces.drivingSide: right (assumed; owner asked to confirm). Lanes sit 0.2 tile right of the centre line; roundabouts circulate anticlockwise from above.

pieceTypes.curve: road-curve 2x2, origin on the shared corner; ports w at (-1,-0.5), s at (0.5,1)
pieceTypes.crossroad: road-crossroad; ports n/e/s/w; all movements except U-turns
pieceTypes.roundabout: road-roundabout 3x3; ports at the middle of each side; single circulating lane at radius 0.8
pieceTypes.ramp: road-slant; w at level 0, e at 0.25 (stack two on a support block for the bridge)
pieceTypes.ramp-steep: road-slant-high; w at 0, e at 0.5 in one tile
pieceTypes.bridge: road-bridge; deck at 0.5; ports n/s (runs along local z)
pieceTypes.split: road-split 1x2, origin on the tile boundary; divided road west (north carriageway out, south carriageway in, two lanes each), single two-way road east; two lanes merge into one
pieceTypes.layby / layby-start / layby-end: road-side / road-side-entry / road-side-exit; lay-by bay on the north side for westbound traffic
pieceTypes.crossing: road-crossing; straight with a pedestrian crossing (traffic calming)
pieceTypes.driveway: road-driveway-single; ports w/e plus a narrow access opening on the south side for local trips
pieceTypes.dead-end / turnaround: road-end / road-end-round; single port e; U-turn
pieceTypes.support: tile-high; no road (elevation block under a raised ramp)

controls.yield: road-sign-warning (no yield sign in the kit)

commands.browserCheck: npm run verify:browser  # requires dev server; or node scripts/verify-browser.mjs <url>
commands.browserCheckHeaded: npm run verify:browser:headed  # same check in a visible Chrome window
